note: Example Blocks is a JS learning submodule of gutenberg (no PHP/config/permissions). It registers two custom Gutenberg blocks via example_blocks.gutenberg.yml: example-blocks/card (client-side, has save.js) and example-blocks/dynamic-card (server-rendered via templates/gutenberg-block--example-blocks--dynamic-card.html.twig). The discovery file declares libraries-edit/libraries-view (example_blocks/blocks), dynamic-blocks (example-blocks/dynamic-card) and custom-blocks under the Media category. The example_blocks/blocks asset library (dist/blocks.js, dist/style-blocks.css) depends on gutenberg/react, gutenberg/block-editor, gutenberg/blocks, gutenberg/components; blocks/index.js calls registerBlockType(). Recipe cases cover the block ids, the static-vs-dynamic distinction, and the registration mechanism. Introspection ensures the module is enabled and reads the blocks it registers. Execution installs the module, verified via the module list and via discovery of its example_blocks/blocks asset library.

evals.prompt: Which Gutenberg blocks does the example_blocks submodule provide?
evals.expected_output: Two blocks: example-blocks/card ('Card') and example-blocks/dynamic-card ('Dynamic Card'), both added to the editor's Media category via example_blocks.gutenberg.yml.

evals.prompt: In the example_blocks submodule, which block is rendered server-side, and how is that server rendering done?
evals.expected_output: example-blocks/dynamic-card is dynamic (listed under dynamic-blocks) and is rendered server-side from templates/gutenberg-block--example-blocks--dynamic-card.html.twig. example-blocks/card is a static block (client-side save.js).

evals.prompt: How does example_blocks register its blocks with Gutenberg and the editor JS, and which libraries do they depend on?
evals.expected_output: It declares them in example_blocks.gutenberg.yml (libraries-edit/libraries-view = example_blocks/blocks, dynamic-blocks, custom-blocks) and registers them in JS with registerBlockType() (blocks/index.js). The example_blocks/blocks library depends on gutenberg/react, gutenberg/block-editor, gutenberg/blocks and gutenberg/components.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the example_blocks submodule and list the custom Gutenberg block ids it registers.
evals.expected_output: It registers example-blocks/card and example-blocks/dynamic-card (see example_blocks.gutenberg.yml on the enabled module).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, which block does the example_blocks submodule render with a server-side Twig template, and what is the template file name?
evals.expected_output: example-blocks/dynamic-card is server-rendered from templates/gutenberg-block--example-blocks--dynamic-card.html.twig (declared under dynamic-blocks in example_blocks.gutenberg.yml).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, make Gutenberg's example blocks (the example_blocks submodule) available by installing/enabling that module. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The example_blocks module is installed/enabled (drush en example_blocks -y), so \Drupal::moduleHandler()->moduleExists('example_blocks') is TRUE.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, ensure the example_blocks submodule's Gutenberg block assets are available — its 'blocks' asset library (example_blocks/blocks) must be discoverable. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable the example_blocks module so its asset library is registered: \Drupal::service('library.discovery')->getLibraryByName('example_blocks','blocks') returns a definition (drush en example_blocks -y).
